title: Council calls on province to end homelessness
subtitle: Culture plan, neighbourhood strategy, community gardens, and two informal public meetings on high-rise zoning applications.
overview: Council called on the Ontario government to acknowledge homelessness as a social, economic and health crisis, commit to ending it, and work with municipalities and partners on an action plan {{vote:m7}}. The motion notes the City is adding $130,000 in 2023 for homelessness initiatives. Copies go to provincial ministers, local MPPs, regional municipalities and the Association of Municipalities of Ontario.

Council approved the culture plan benchmarking report {{vote:m4}} and a new Community Garden Program Policy {{vote:m6}}. It received the neighbourhood strategy report {{vote:m5}} and the 2023 community cash grants report {{vote:m3}}; a councillor declared a conflict on the grants item and did not vote. Council also passed by-laws establishing and widening public highways at Cedarbrae Avenue, Glen Forrest Boulevard and University Avenue East, along with the confirming by-law {{vote:m8}}.

Two informal public meetings covered rezoning applications for 20 University Avenue East and 143 Columbia Street West. No decisions were made, and staff will report back at a formal public meeting. Council also heard from an agriculture federation delegate and held a closed session earlier in the day.

decisions.item: Call on province to end homelessness
decisions.detail: Council asked the provincial government to urgently acknowledge the crisis, commit to ending homelessness and work with municipalities on an action plan {{vote:m7}}.
Council approved report CAO2023-001 and agreed to keep championing local cultural development {{vote:m4}}.
Council approved report COM2023-002 and Corporate Policy M-012, which sets out how neighbourhood-led community gardens on City land are supported {{vote:m6}}.
Council received the report on neighbourhood strategy work and supports in 2022 for information {{vote:m5}}.
Council received the 2023 community cash grants report for information only, with one councillor absent for the vote after declaring a conflict {{vote:m3}}.

debate: On homelessness, the mover said the City and Region are already responding strongly. They argued the municipal tax base was not designed to fund social services, and that the province needs to fund housing, mental health and addictions services before its budget.

On the University Avenue East proposal, councillors asked about reduced residential parking, noting that the traffic study appeared to cite a different parking number than the application. They also asked about pick-up and drop-off traffic on the street. The applicant's planners said the reduction fits a transit-served location and a smaller podium.

Councillors questioned how geothermal wells could work on sites with a high water table and contamination. The applicant's planners said the zoning change only opens the door, and that regional approvals and technical work are still needed.

A resident asked about trees and green space, and whether the all one-bedroom unit mix could later be changed. Councillors raised unit variety, affordability, accessible units and tenant relocation at the Columbia Street site. The applicant's planners said their portfolio diversifies unit types across projects and that affordable housing would be better delivered in a larger future project.

In the culture plan discussion, councillors raised safety and street closures for Lumen after attendance well above expectations, and asked about events outside Uptown. Staff said suitable event spaces elsewhere are limited and a pop-up series is planned. On community gardens, staff said neighbourhood work is limited by small staff capacity.
